content:
Samsung recently launched the One UI 9.5 beta for the Galaxy S26 series. Today some strings in that software point to two new Camera app features in the works, called Vision mode and Auto portrait.
Vision would be a new mode sitting alongside Photo, Video, and the rest. It appears to show an AI-written summary of what's in front of you, along with tappable keywords and two buttons next to the shutter, Ask and Translate. If that sounds familiar, it's because Apple did something very similar with iOS 27, which moved Visual Intelligence into the Camera app as a new Siri mode next to Photo and Video, also with a description card at the top of the viewfinder and two buttons on either side of the shutter.
In Samsung's case, tapping Ask, or one of the keywords, would send the camera frame to Gemini, while Translate would hand it off to Samsung's AI Vision app, which is basically what's left of Bixby Vision. Pressing the shutter reportedly won't save a photo. It will only freeze the preview so you can keep asking questions about it. Below the summary card, Vision mode will also offer suggested actions, a text extraction button, and a flashlight toggle.
The live preview is apparently streamed to a new Samsung app called Visual Agent Service, which isn't available on the S26 family yet, so it's unclear whether the scene summary is generated on the phone or in the cloud. You can already do much of what Vision mode offers by sharing your camera with Gemini Live, but Samsung's version would be built right into the Camera app, with its own scene summary before you reach Gemini.
The other feature, called Auto portrait, appears to apply background blur automatically in Photo mode when it detects a face or a pet. You could also turn it on manually from the viewfinder and adjust the blur with a slider.
Neither feature currently works on the S26 devices, and the discovered code suggests both need hardware these phones don’t have, so they will likely have to wait for the upcoming Galaxy S27 handsets, which are rumored to launch early next year.
